name: Dagster (run storage, schedule/sensor ticks, event log)
param_style: SQLAlchemy Core (1.x/2.x compat layer) on the sqlite dialect; ? positional, IN lists expanded per call; DateTime binds as ISO strings
schema_source: python_modules/dagster/dagster/_core/storage/{runs,schedules,event_log}/schema.py, created by the pinned SqliteRunStorage/SqliteScheduleStorage/SqliteEventLogStorage and dumped from sqlite_master; the three databases (runs.db, schedules.db, event log index shard) share one file here
data_scale: scale 1: one code location, 11 sensors (two tick every 30 s) and 6 schedules over 45 days; 3.5k runs with 15k run_tags, 132k event_logs (incl. ~20k asset materializations/observations), 15k asset_event_tags, 65 assets (24 daily-partitioned, ~410 partitions on the backfilled one), 6.2k asset check executions, 57k job_ticks (SKIPPED sensor ticks kept 7 days, SUCCESS/FAILURE and schedule ticks forever, Dagster's default retention). Event/tick bodies are trimmed serdes JSON (~450 B). ~160 MB. --scale N multiplies the history days (runs, events, partitions, checks grow ~N x) and makes the two fastest sensors tick every 30/N s (skipped ticks grow ~N x within the fixed 7-day retention)
visibility_note: 16k stars; SQLite is the default storage for dagster dev and local/single-node deployments (DAGSTER_HOME with runs.db, schedules.db, history/)
interest_note: Tick lookups with an OR that defeats the (selector_id, timestamp) index; a rank() window over every tick of every sensor for the Automation page; runs filtered by self-joins on run_tags then sorted by id; partition status via GROUP BY max(id) subqueries joined back to event_logs and asset_event_tags; window-ranked data versions per partition.
reach_note: widely self-hosted orchestrator; SQLite is the out-of-the-box storage, while larger production deployments move to Postgres

cpu_evidence.summary: SQLite, sensors ticking every 10 s for months: Automation page takes 3-6 min to load Last Tick/Last Run, single sensor page stuck >10 min
Sensors can't load: the runs-by-sensor-tag self-join (LIMIT 1) and the OR tick query hit statement timeouts with ~20 sensors (Postgres)
Sensor page GraphQL error: the latest-tick query (selector_id = ? OR selector_id IS NULL AND job_origin_id = ?) times out (Postgres)
The OR in _ticks_query forces a fetch-and-sort of every tick of an instigator; >90 s with 405k ticks (35k for one schedule), delaying the scheduler 2-15 min
Job partitions page with ~33k hourly partitions takes over 90 s to load
